chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Fudayl said: A Sindian slave said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

I told my master, 'Sell me for seven hundred dirhams, and I will give you three hundred [dirhams].' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'If you had money on the day you made the condition, then it is upon you to give it; and if you did not have money on that day, then there is nothing upon you.'

key_terms.فَعَلَيْكَ أَنْ تُعْطِيَهُ: Then it is upon you to give it
key_terms.فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ شَيْ ءٌ: Then there is nothing upon you
key_terms.يَوْمَ شَرَطْتَ: On the day you made the condition

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave buying himself if he lacks the funds at the time of the agreement?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the principle of conditional obligation (*shart*) in the contract of self-purchase (*mudabbad*), emphasizing that the slave's liability is contingent upon his financial status at the moment the agreement was struck. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that if the slave possessed the means when the condition was set, he is bound to pay, whereas lack of funds at that specific time exempts him, reflecting the Shia juristic focus on fairness and capacity in contractual duties.
